newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers but seen weak vs dollar.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers but seen weak vs dollar.

text.p: * Ringgit recovered after dollar's failure to test 2.5250
* Seen falling back on dollar bids by offshore players
* Fears of central bank intervention and local corporate selling around 2.5240 expected to cap dollar's rise
The ringgit recovered against the dollar in early Asian trading but the Malaysian currency was expected to remain under pressure from offshore bids for the dollar, dealers said.
They said players were cashing in profits after the dollar/ringgit failed to test the 2.5250 level.
"But there are fresh orders to buy dollar around 2.5220 from offshore players," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur. "With the dollar still biddish, it should test higher levels again today."
Dealers said some offshore parties were buying the dollar ahead of the mid-year book closing.
But dealers said fears of central bank intervention and corporate selling out of Kuala Lumpur could again cap the dollar's topside at 2.5240/50.
"We have some orders from local corporates to sell dollar around 2.5240," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara's presence was not detected on Wednesday.
Dealers said they expected some caution as the system may turn tight. Some two billion ringgit from a Bank Negara lending maturity is said to leave the market on Thursday.
At 0230 GMT, ringgit was quoted at 2.5217/27 a dollar. It closed at 2.5232/42 in Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday.
